newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas grains harvesting advances on dry weather.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas grains harvesting advances on dry weather.

text.p: Grains and soybean harvesting advanced in the week ended Sunday in Arkansas with few problems reported amid mostly cool and dry weather conditions, according to the Arkansas Agricultural Statistics Service.
Corn harvest neared completion at 99 percent, just above 98 percent a year ago and equal to the five-year average.
Soybean combining as of Sunday stood at 38 percent complete, behind the 46 percent a year ago and above the average pace of 35 percent.
Rice harvest was 98 percent finished, ahead 95 percent a year ago and also ahead of the 93 percent average.
Cotton harvest was 68 percent complete, behind 70 percent a year ago and up from the 60 percent average pace.

Wheat was 34 percent planted, slightly ahead of 32 percent a year ago and the 31 percent average pace. Eleven percent of the crop had emerged, up from 10 percent a year ago but below the 15 percent average pace.
